card.name: Digits inside numbers before units
card.fires_on: A single digit (or the X of XOR) in the middle of a number or term, typically just before a unit such as ppm, mg, psi, MAC or IU/mL. The number is usually still unfinished, as in 0.5, 30 or 600.

modes.label: Decimal digit
modes.description: The digit after a decimal point in a concentration or dose value.
modes.example: reaches 0.<<5>> ppm when measured in the breathing circuit,

modes.label: Digit in a whole number
modes.description: A digit within a larger dose, rate or pressure figure, often a trailing zero.

modes.label: Opening digit after a bracket
modes.description: The first digit of a figure in parentheses, such as a percentage or dose.

card.plain: It fires on a digit partway through a number that is followed by a unit, like the 5 in 0.5 ppm.
